audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL logic. EL topics include EVM jump destination validation (Cancun runtime), stack overflow/underflow protection, BLOBBASEFEE opcode (EIP-7516), contract code size limits (EIP-170), bn128 pairing precompile (EIP-197), Petersburg hardfork activation (EIP-1716), gas limit cap RPC discovery (EIP-8123), and Merkle proof generation/verification (EIP-1186). CL topics include Gloas fork choice with dual-track payload state management, PTC voting, and proposer boost conditions.

in_scope: EVM Stack Operations and Bounds Checking
Gloas Fork Choice: Dual-Track Payload States

misclassified_entities.reason: Governance entity, not a runtime data source. The All Core Devs group makes decisions about protocol changes but does not send data into the running system at runtime. This is a process/governance entity, not a trust boundary actor.
Governance entity, not a runtime data source. EIP authors propose protocol changes through the governance process but do not interact with the running system as an external entity.
Development entity, not a runtime data source. Client implementation teams build software but do not send data into the running system at runtime.

When the audit scope includes both EL and CL, the Execution Layer is an in-scope target component, not an external entity. However, from the CL's perspective, the EL communicates via the Engine API and should be modeled as an interlocutor. Re-classified as EXT-EL-VIA-ENGINE-API below.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit signed beacon blocks via P2P gossip. Any validator can propose, and proposals may be malicious (invalid blocks, equivocating proposals). Data is unauthenticated at the network level; signature verification is part of the processing. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER and EXT-PROPOSER from the Gloas fork choice subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: PTC Committee Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: PTC validators submit payload timeliness attestations via gossip. A colluding majority (>256 of 512) could manipulate fork choice between FULL and EMPTY tracks. Individual attestations cannot be trusted without committee-level threshold verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The EL provides execution payload envelopes to the CL via the Engine API, authenticated with JWT. The channel is authenticated but payload content (transaction results, state roots) must still be validated. Relevant for Gloas dual-track payload state management.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit contract creation transactions. The init code and resulting bytecode are fully attacker-controlled. EIP-170 size limits prevent DoS via oversized contracts. Covers EXT-DEPLOYER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks containing contract creations and transactions. Blocks may contain invalid transactions or be crafted to exploit verification overhead. Covers EXT-NETWORK from EIP-170.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and wallets interact via JSON-RPC to query gas caps, request Merkle proofs, and submit transactions. RPC input is unauthenticated and potentially malicious. Covers EXT-USER and EXT-RPC-CLIENT.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted RPC Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From a light client or verifier perspective, the RPC provider returning proof data or gas cap info is untrusted. Proof data must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot. Covers EXT-RPC-PROVIDER and EXT-RPC-NODE.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL sends execution payloads and fork choice updates to the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. While the channel is authenticated, payload content (block data, state transitions) must be fully validated by the EL. This is the archetypal SEMI_TRUSTED boundary for EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode to precompiles (address 0x8 for bn128 pairing)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can call precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input must be rigorously validated (length, point encoding, subgroup membership). Covers EXT-EVM-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer / Light Client Sync
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain sync / light client protocol (trusted block headers)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Provides trusted block headers used as trust anchors for Merkle proof verification. The consensus mechanism provides cryptoeconomic guarantees but is not infallible. Covers EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER from EIP-1186.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block must pass signature verification, slot validation, parent existence check, and state transition validation before being accepted into fork choice. Equivocating proposers must be detected.

PTC attestations must verify: validator is in assigned PTC committee for the slot, attestation signature is valid, and validator index maps correctly to ptc_vote boolean vector. Quorum threshold (>256/512) required before payload timeliness is accepted.

Execution payload envelope must be verified for data availability (blob KZG commitments). JWT authentication validates the channel but payload content integrity must be checked independently. Payload must correspond to a known block.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, init code execution, and returned bytecode size check (<=24576 bytes per EIP-170). Out-of-gas on size violation.
Blocks from P2P must be fully validated: header verification, transaction execution, state root comparison, contract size limits enforcement. Size-bounded verification time guaranteed by EIP-170.

All RPC inputs must be validated: address format, storage key format, block identifier resolution, parameter bounds. Rate limiting and request size limits should prevent DoS. Storage key count for eth_getProof should be bounded.

Proof data from untrusted RPC providers must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot. Each node in accountProof and storageProof must be hashed and path-validated. Non-existence proofs must show divergence or empty branch.

JWT authentication required on the channel. Payload content must be fully validated: transaction execution, state root computation, gas accounting, receipt verification. The EL must not trust CL-provided execution data without independent verification.

Input must be validated: length divisible by 192, G1 coordinates < p and on curve (or zero point), G2 coordinates valid in F_p² with correct subgroup order q. Gas cost (80000*k + 100000) must be pre-deducted. Invalid input must revert consuming all gas.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header sync (light client protocol / beacon chain)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block headers are trusted based on consensus mechanism (PoS finality). The stateRoot in the header serves as the cryptographic trust anchor. Light client sync protocol must verify committee signatures and finality checkpoints.
